set.body:
Problem: the current mixed-TR receipt uses tools/r-parity/mixed-tr-reference-lock.json, while validate_manifest.py assumes tools/r-parity/reference-lock.json; check_receipts.py already accepts the checked-in generator output. Related fixture/generator files contain user work: inspect their diff and coordinate before editing.
Files: tools/scenarios/validate_manifest.py and its stdlib tests; inspect tools/r-parity/receipt_tools.py, mixed-tr-reference-lock.json, and docs/scenarios/fixtures/fit.mixed-tr-fixed-effects.v1.r.json.
Steps: treat the receipt's declared lock_path as the selected reference environment, using the existing receipt-tools convention. Require a repository-local approved lock file, validate its actual SHA-256 and required revisions, and compare source revisions with THAT lock. Retain the default lock behavior for every other fixture. No blanket skip for custom locks.
Acceptance: tests cover default and mixed-TR locks, wrong SHA, wrong package revision, missing file and path escape. Run python3 -S tools/scenarios/validate_manifest.py, python3 -S tools/r-parity/check_receipts.py, and the validator/receipt stdlib unit tests. All manifest/receipt checks must pass together after P4.4b; retain the adopted numerical outputs and tolerances unchanged.
set.title: P4.4c: validate the declared mixed-TR reference lock without weakening receipt checks
